questions.explain: Unlike some other engines, RDS for SQL Server has no IAM database authentication path — SQL logins and Windows auth via Managed AD are the options.
options: RDS for SQL Server supports IAM token-based database logins natively
RDS for SQL Server does not support IAM database authentication — there is no token-based login, so plan accordingly
IAM database authentication works on RDS for SQL Server only when joined to Managed AD
RDS Proxy adds IAM database authentication for SQL Server automatically
questions.q: Which statement about IAM database authentication on RDS for SQL Server is correct?

questions.explain: Entra-only mode disables SQL authentication completely, so only Entra ID identities can connect — removing password-based attack surface.
options: It disables SQL authentication entirely, eliminating the password-spray attack surface
It converts all existing SQL logins into contained database users
It requires MFA only for application connections, not human logins
It enables Kerberos authentication for Managed Instance listeners
questions.q: What does enabling Entra-only authentication mode on an Azure SQL server do?

questions.explain: The rotation that breaks the application's connection pool is discovered at 2 AM unless rehearsed — test rotation in staging first.
options: Because Azure Key Vault rotation requires a manual approval in staging
Because Secrets Manager cannot rotate RDS credentials without a staging rehearsal
Because applications that read the secret at startup may hold the old password and break their connection pool
Because dual-password rotation is unsupported outside of staging
questions.q: Why should secret rotation be tested in staging before rotation day?

questions.explain: The AG listener and each replica need proper SPNs registered — the classic Kerberos failure, now in the cloud.
options: Using constrained delegation instead of unconstrained delegation for double-hop scenarios
Relying on NTLM fallback when the SPN check fails
Kerberos tolerating 5 minutes of time skew between domain controllers
Missing or incorrect Service Principal Names registered for the AG listener and each replica
questions.q: What is the classic Kerberos failure for Always On AGs in the cloud?

questions.explain: The diagnostic order never changes: network, then credential validity, then identity provider, then authorization.
options: Credential validity, then network, then authorization, then identity provider
Authorization, then identity provider, then network, then credential validity
Network, then credential validity, then identity provider, then authorization
Identity provider, then network, then credential validity, then authorization
questions.q: What is the correct diagnostic order when troubleshooting an authentication failure?
